body: I had `* real_t(1.0 / 3.0)` here to ensure that this is implemented as a multiplication instead of a divsion. We're in a hot path here because we're looping over all faces in the SB. Multiplications are much faster than divisions.
I had `1.0e-6` here, `CMP_EPSILON` is `1.0e-5`. This means that a triangle with edges shorter than 3 mm will no longer receive an impulse (previously the cutoff was at 1 mm).
I had `* real(0.5)` because of reasons mentioned above.

I was collecting the areas that have wind pressure outside of the loop. We're doing an extra check per soft body  face now to check if the area has wind pressure, instead of only doing the check once per area.
It would help to add some documentation on what the return value of this function means

Maybe this is a silly stance on my part, and I realize `GodotSoftBody3D` was doing something similar already, but this kind of optimization looks a bit out-of-place in Godot in general. It's something I would expect more aggressive compiler optimization flags to do automatically for you instead, although I realize they usually bring other problems along with them as well.

Anyway, I've put back the multiplication.
That was indeed a mistake on my part.

The memory allocation(s) from the `LocalVector` frankly bothered me more than the extra check. I figured you're likely not going to have more than a couple of area overlaps anyway.

Using something like `JPH::Array` with `JPH::STLLocalAllocator` for some arbitrary amount of likely wind areas would be better I guess, but not using Godot's own containers always feels wrong, and they sadly lack an equivalent to it.

Anyway, I guess I can't justify the change without actual profiling anyway, so I've put back the `LocalVector`.
It seems fine when testing it, so I went ahead and pushed it, but let me know if it looks off for any reason.
